distribution.name: fig10_fossils.pdf
distribution.description: Fig. 10: (a) Composite mould of left valve of Pteria murchisoni (Geinitz, 1861) with coarse growth lines, bed 16; GZG.STR.84027. (b) Steinkern of cephalothorax and thoracetron of Limulitella sp.; bed 16; GZG.STR.84074. (c) Composite mould of cephalothorax of Limulitella sp. and composite mould of left valve of Pteria murchisoni; bed 16; GZG.STR.84080 (photographs: MLH).

distribution.name: fig11_ripple-plots.jpg
distribution.description: Fig. 11: Ripple measurements (N = 100) from three layers of the Volpriehausen Formation. (a) RSI versus RI diagram after Tanner (1967). (b) Ripple height versus ripple length diagram for ripple length ≥45 mm (N = 62) after Reineck & Wunderlich (1968). Blue circles: layer r1, green triangles: layer r2, orange squares: layer r3. Measurements see Table 2 in the Appendix and in Göttingen Research Online Data repository (https://doi.org/10.25625/WEEWSX).

distribution.name: fig12_polished-sections.pdf
distribution.description: Fig. 12: Polished sections of samples from bed 16. (a) Sample l16p1a, visible arched lamination due to orientation of mica flakes. (b) Sample l16p1b. (c) Detailed view of polished section l16p1a. Note the discordant layering in the lower righthand corner. (d) Detailed view of polished section l16p1b. Note the different phases of layering (photographs: MLH).

distribution.name: fig1_Steinkerne murchisoni.pdf
distribution.description: Fig. 1: Characteristic occurrence of Pteria murchisoni in the Volpriehausen Formation (Buntsandstein): poorly preserved internal and external moulds with few characteristics in a relatively coarsegrained sandstone matrix. Heidelbeerenberg (Blueberry Hill), northeast of Volkmarsen-Ehringen, map sheet Wolfhagen, northern Hesse, Germany (Hessisches Landesamt für Naturschutz, Umwelt und Geologie, Wiesbaden, coll. no. 42.11.03). Length of largest specimen (centre) ca. 12 mm (photograph: MRWA).

distribution.name: fig2_buntsandstein-outcrop.pdf
distribution.description: Fig. 2: (a) Outcrop of the Buntsandstein (brown) and the Middle Buntsandstein (orange) in Germany; red rectangle: position of geological map area of the Hildesheim Forest in Fig. 2b. Data from Toloczyki et al. (2006), German Stratigraphic Commission (2016), GeoBasis-DE / BKG (2020a), GeoBasis-DE / BKG (2020b). (b) Simplified geological map of the Hildesheim Forest area and position of the studied locality. Abbreviations: kr – Cretaceous, j – Jurassic, k – Keuper, m – Muschelkalk, su – Lower Buntsandstein, sm – Middle Buntsandstein, so – Upper Buntsandstein (map: MLH [a], GA [b]).

distribution.name: fig3_paleogeography.jpg
distribution.description: Fig. 3: Palaeogeographical overview of the Central European Basin (CEB) in the Early Triassic (‘Buntsandstein time’). White – area of denudation, light grey – marginal facies, dark grey – basin facies, 1 – Northern North Sea Basin, 2 – Central Graben, 3 – Rynkøbing-Fyn High, 4 – Horn Graben, 5 – Glückstadt Graben, 6 – Silesian-Moravian Gate, 7 – East-Carpathian Gate. Inset map shows location of the CEB (rectangle) in Pangaea for the Early Triassic. T – Tethys. After Ziegler (1990), Bachmann et al. (2010), Röhling & Lepper (2013), Wolfram Research (2020) (map: MLH).

distribution.name: fig4_buntsandstein-stratigraphy.jpg
distribution.description: Fig. 4: Comparative stratigraphy of the Volpriehausen and Detfurth formations in Hesse and southern Lower Saxony (central Germany): the thickness of the fluvial ‘Volpriehausen Sandstein’ is relatively constant from south to north. The ‘Volpriehausen Wechselfolge’, on the other hand, increases in thickness and is more differentiated as it approaches the foreland of the North German Basin. The ‘Avicula-Schichten’ are separated in northern Hesse and northwards only but not developed in central Hesse and southwards (from Tietze 2021b, modified; Lepper et al. 2013).

distribution.name: fig5_outcrop.pdf
distribution.description: Fig. 5: (a) Composite view of the upper Volpriehausen Formation and basal Detfurth Formation in the Röderhof outcrop. (b, c) Centre of detailed section (Figs 6–8), white arrows indicate bed 19, red arrow points at a large specimen of Pteria murchisoni (sketch: GA, photographs: MLH).

Fig. 6: Columnar section of the central part of the Röderhof section (N 52.080369, E 9.981922), showing the pteriid-limulid beds (beds 15
and 16) in the upper part of the Volpriehausen Formation (artwork: MLH).

distribution.name: fig7_beds.pdf
distribution.description: Fig. 7: Röderhof section, central part, top views of selected beds. (a) Bed 16 with indistinct ripples. (b) Bed 18a with interference ripples. (c) Bed 18b with linguid ripples. (d) Bed 18c with symmetrical wave ripples (photographs: MLH).

distribution.name: fig8_beds.pdf
distribution.description: Fig. 8: Röderhof section, central part, top views of selected beds. (a) Bed 19 with asymmetrical wave ripples. White dashed outline: parts for ripple measurements (see Table 2 in Appendix and in Göttingen Research Online Data repository https://doi.org/10.25625/WEEWSX). (b) Bed 20 with synaeresis cracks (photographs: MLH).
